summary: Defines the problem statement, scope, and protocol requirements for Network Endpoint Assessment, a way for network owners to check the posture of a system when it requests access or later. Posture may include whether anti-virus or a host firewall is present and current. It also introduces a reference model and terminology. It is informational.

eli5.summary: Before letting a visitor in, a building checks that they are healthy. NEA checks a computer's safety, like having up-to-date protection, before or while it joins.

subtitle: The problem statement, reference model and protocol requirements for checking the security posture of a device that wants on a network.

tldr.problem: Network owners want to know whether an endpoint has working anti-virus, a host firewall and current patches before or while it is on the network, but existing vendor architectures do not interoperate.
tldr.mechanism: Network Endpoint Assessment (NEA) defines a client and server reference model with three layered protocols (PA, PB and PT) and lists the requirements candidate protocols must meet.
tldr.outcome: The RFC is informational context and requirements for the NEA Working Group, not a protocol. It also covers security and privacy concerns, such as lying endpoints and over-disclosure of posture.

facts.label: Requirement groups
facts.value: Common (C-1 to C-11), PA, PB, PT

today: RFC 5209 is an Informational document, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It records the NEA problem statement, reference model and requirements rather than defining a protocol.

sections.title: The Problem NEA Addresses
sections.content:
Endpoints on a network face many threats, and some protection comes from making sure they conform to security policies. Network Endpoint Assessment (NEA) checks an endpoint's posture, meaning the configuration and status of its hardware and software as it relates to security policy. If a system lacks a host-based firewall, anti-virus software or critical security patches, NEA lets the network detect that and indicate remediation steps. A compliant endpoint may still be vulnerable to threats on the network.

Without NEA, keeping endpoints compliant is time-consuming and difficult. Not all endpoints are managed by corporate IT, such as lab assets and contractor machines, and laptops may miss updates because they are not permanently attached. With NEA the network can assess an endpoint as soon as it asks for access or at any time afterwards.

The RFC names several uses: checking compliance on connect, reassessment later (for example, if a user disables the firewall), supplementing asset inventory data, and service-triggered assessment for mission critical applications. Similar architectures already existed in products (Trusted Network Connect, Network Access Protection and Network Admission Control) but did not offer adequate interoperability.
sections.eli5: Offices have laptops that wander in and out. NEA lets the office quickly check each one has its protection switched on, instead of hoping for the best.

sections.title: Scope and Where NEA Applies
sections.content:
The Working Group's priority is the two higher-layer protocols, the Posture Attribute (PA) and Posture Broker (PB) protocols, designed to be carried over a variety of Posture Transport (PT) protocols. With a standard PT such as EAP or TLS, a NEA Client from one vendor should work with a NEA Server from another.

Out of scope are enforcement of restricted network access, remediation protocols, communication with remote collectors or validators, one client reporting posture for other endpoints, defining what triggers an assessment, and detecting lying endpoints.

NEA is aimed at cases where the endpoint owner is also the network owner, such as an enterprise issuing equipment to employees, or where the endpoint owner has agreed to follow the network's policies, such as a contractor with a personal laptop. It is not expected to apply in places like a coffee shop, where an assessment could amount to an invasion of privacy.
sections.eli5: A school can check its own school computers, and a guest who agreed to the rules. A cafe has no business poking around inside a customer's laptop.

sections.title: The Reference Model
sections.content:
The model splits into a NEA Client on the endpoint and a NEA Server on the network side, joined by three layered protocols.

  • Posture Collectors (client) gather facts such as OS version, patch level, anti-virus and firewall status. They first consult local privacy policy about what may be disclosed.
  • Posture Validators (server) assess one or more features, create results and, if needed, remediation instructions, or ask for more attributes.
  • The Posture Broker Client and Posture Broker Server multiplex and de-multiplex messages between collectors and validators. The server side also computes the global assessment decision.
  • The Posture Transport Client and Server set up a reliable channel and provide cryptographic protection for the dialog.

PA is a lightweight wrapper around a set of attributes, carried inside PB. PB batches messages and carries the global decision. PT carries the PB messages during the connection request or after connectivity is established. During network connection, PT may be constrained (limited MTU, few round trips, low bandwidth), so a full reassessment can follow later.
sections.eli5: On the computer, little helpers each check one thing, like a nurse checking temperature. A messenger bundles their answers and sends them to the network, where matching helpers decide if everything looks fine.

sections.title: Attributes and Use Cases
sections.content:
Attributes are the nouns of an assessment, and the server can only ask about things that have a defined attribute. The RFC classes them as Posture (observed configuration), Request (what the server wants), Result (the decision), Remediation (how to fix things) and Assertion (reusable proof of a recent compliant assessment, such as a signed and dated item). The Working Group will standardize some attributes; others are vendor-specific.

The use cases fall into two groups. An initial assessment may be triggered by joining a network, requesting a service, or the endpoint itself. In one example an office desktop lacking a recent patch is put on a restricted network, follows remediation instructions, and is admitted after a new assessment. A reassessment can be triggered by the client (for example, monitoring software notices the firewall was switched off) or by the server (for example, an urgent patch advisory), and assertions let a client skip resending detailed posture.
sections.eli5: The network asks questions, the computer answers, and a pass can be stamped so it need not answer everything again next time.

sections.title: Protocol Requirements
sections.content:
The requirements are used to compare candidate protocols. They describe features a protocol must be capable of offering; they do not force a deployer to use every one.

  • Common: multiple round trips in one assessment (C-1) and protection against active and passive attacks including replay (C-3). PA and PB must work over any PT (C-4), existing open standards should be reused (C-5), and strings must support UTF-8 (C-10).
  • PA: extensible standard attributes and vendor-specific namespaces (PA-1, PA-2), and end-to-end authentication, integrity and confidentiality (PA-5).
  • PB: must not interpret PA contents (PB-2), must carry identifiers for routing (PB-3), and must work over a half-duplex PT (PB-4).
  • PT: mutual authentication, integrity, confidentiality and replay protection (PT-2), reliable delivery (PT-3), and ability to run over 802.1X and IKEv2 (PT-4).
sections.eli5: This is a checklist the future messenger systems have to pass: be safe from snoopers, work in many places, and deliver every message in order.

sections.title: Security and Privacy Considerations
sections.content:
NEA trusts the endpoint to report honestly. The model does not detect lying endpoints or malware that tricks collectors, so a compromised system may pass an assessment. The network between client and server is not assumed trustworthy, so protocols must resist man-in-the-middle attacks, message modification and replay. For example, a non-compliant machine might relay posture fetched from a clean endpoint, so the RFC prefers a cryptographic binding between posture and the authenticated session.

NEA also raises privacy risks, because it gives a network visibility into an endpoint. The RFC encourages opt-in per user and per server, asking only for specific attributes rather than wildcards, user notification or logging of disallowed requests, and a disclosure statement from the server. It describes three disclosure models: send everything, a pre-provisioned list, or the server requesting attributes during the exchange.
sections.eli5: A guard can only trust what the visitor says about being healthy, and the visitor should only have to answer the questions that really matter.

layers.label: PA: Posture Attribute
layers.detail: Posture Collectors talk to Posture Validators

layers.label: PB: Posture Broker
layers.detail: Batches PA messages between the brokers and carries the global decision

layers.label: PT: Posture Transport
layers.detail: Reliable, protected channel between NEA Client and NEA Server

items.title: Posture
items.text: Observed configuration or status of an endpoint feature.

items.title: Request
items.text: What posture information the server wants.

items.title: Result
items.text: The compliance decision, per feature or global.

items.title: Assertion
items.text: Reusable proof of a prior compliant assessment.
